newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council members condemn Bosnian Serb attacks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council members condemn Bosnian Serb attacks.

text.p: Security Council members Wednesday strongly condemned recent attacks against international personnel in the Bosnian Serb region of Bosnia and called on authorities there to bring the culprits to justice.

A statement read to reporters by council President Peter Osvald of Sweden was prompted by a series of small-scale bomb attacks that followed a raid by troops of the NATO-led peace Stabilisation Force (SFOR) on Serbs wanted by the U.N. war crimes tribunal.

"Members of the Security Council condemn in the strongest terms possible the attacks against the personnel of SFOR, the U.N. International Police Task Force (IPFT) and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE)," the statement said.
"Council members call upon the authorities of Republika Srbska (the Bosnian Serb Republic) to investigate these actions and to bring to justice those responsible."
Council members also urged the authorities to protect international personnel.
